transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I'm just losing hours every day to rechecking things. It's... it's stuff like my dressing supplies, the door locks, and even work stuff, like file dimensions or my revision notes. I just don't feel allowed to move on to the next thing until I've gone through the exact same routine enough times. I basically have to keep doing it until the anxiety finally drops.
When you're going through this checking, do you feel that it's excessive or doesn't really make sense, or does it feel like a reasonable and necessary thing to do?

I definitely know it's excessive. Um, logically, it doesn't make any sense at all. Like, I know the door is locked because I just checked it two minutes ago, or I know the file is right. 

But in the moment... it just feels completely necessary. My brain kind of tells me I have to do it, and if I don't, the anxiety just won't go away. So, yeah, I know it's unreasonable to spend hours on this stuff, but I still feel like I have to do it anyway.

Aside from the urge to check, do you also experience specific intrusive thoughts or images—like a fear that something terrible will happen—that trigger the need to check, or is it more just a general anxious feeling without a specific thought attached?

It's definitely tied to specific thoughts. It's not just a general feeling. Um, like with my dressing supplies... even after I know I've cleaned the wound area perfectly, this thought just cuts in that I missed one tiny thing. And my brain tells me it's going to turn into a massive infection. 

It happens at work, too. I'm an engineer, so I work with CAD files a lot. Even after I've reviewed a file, I get this intense fear that I made a tiny design mistake, and because of that, something is going to fail and someone is going to get hurt. I try to tell myself it's fine, but I just can't reason it away. The thought just stays there until I check again.
How long have you been dealing with this checking behavior—weeks, months, or longer?

Um, to be honest, I'm not exactly sure. I haven't really kept track of a timeline. It's hard to pinpoint exactly when it started getting this bad, or when it really began... so I couldn't really tell you if it's been a certain number of weeks or months. I just haven't really noticed the exact timeframe.
On a typical day, roughly how many hours would you say you spend on all this checking and rechecking combined?

I'd say I'm losing hours every day to it. Honestly, that's really what brings me in here. I'm just spending so much time rechecking things—my dressing supplies, the door locks at home, and then at work, checking the file dimensions and revision notes over and over. I basically just don't feel allowed to move on until I've gone through that same routine enough times that the anxiety finally drops. So, yeah, combined, it's definitely hours out of my day.

Even though you're not sure of the exact date it started, can you tell me approximately how long you've felt these checking behaviors have been a significant problem—would you say it's been more than six months, or less?

Um, I really couldn't say if it's been more or less than six months. It kind of just... crept up on me, I guess. I know it's a major issue right now, but I don't have a clear memory of when it actually crossed the line into taking up so much of my time. So, yeah, I really just don't know.

Can you think of any specific event or change in your life—like starting a new job, moving, or a stressful situation—that happened around the time you first noticed these checking behaviors becoming a problem?

Um... no, not really. I've tried to think if there was some kind of trigger, but nothing really comes to mind. I haven't moved recently, and work has been pretty standard for a while, so it wasn't a new job or anything like that. There wasn't a big stressful event that I can point to, either. It just sort of... slowly built up over time, I guess, without me really noticing a specific starting point.
Would you say these checking behaviors have caused noticeable problems in your daily life—like being late to work, conflict with family, or feeling distressed about the time it takes?

Yeah, it's definitely causing problems. Um, at work, my project deadlines have started slipping. I end up staying late just trying to get comfortable enough with the files to actually submit them. And outside of work... well, I've pretty much stopped making it to my paddleboarding meetups, and I don't really work out anymore either. The checking routines just eat up all the time I used to have for myself. So, yeah, it's getting in the way of a lot.
